Recent work supports validating diagnostics through metamorphic relations and mutation testing. A [2024 recommender study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) demonstrated oracle-free reliability testing across LibRec, PREA and Surprise; its evidence does not directly establish HSTU-specific invariants. A [2025 study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807) combines metamorphic-relation selection with mutation testing to assess fault detection and sensitivity. [ISVMT (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107944) applies similar reasoning to validating diagnostic indicators themselves.

Applied to this HSTU checkpoint, a proposed suite would check deterministic no-op/reload equivalence; candidate permutation followed by inverse permutation; unchanged prefix features when only future tokens change; and left-padding equivalence only when effective positions, timestamps and normalization remain equivalent. Verify readout against the actual final nonpadding index. Run in evaluation mode with numerical tolerances; PyTorch documents that [functional SDPA still applies dropout when dropout_p is positive](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention), even during evaluation. These are proposed implementation checks, not published HSTU validation results.

Inject isolated defects into temporary copies of the same model: disable causal masking, expose padding, substitute count−1 readout, or misalign candidate IDs and scores. Record a probe-by-defect detection matrix, detection rates for applicable non-equivalent mutations, false alarms on equivalent controls, numerical deviations and runtime. Exclude equivalent or unexercised mutations from detection denominators. This tests diagnostic validity without fitting additional predictors; passing establishes only the exercised properties, not recommendation quality or improved validation HR@10.
